source.text: מִזְמ֗וֹר לְדָ֫וִ֥דיְהוָ֣ה קְ֭רָאתִיךָ ח֣וּשָׁה לִּ֑י הַאֲזִ֥ינָה ק֝וֹלִ֗י בְּקָרְאִי־לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: A psalm of David. YHWH, I call to you; hurry to me; give ear to my voice when I call to you.

en.L: A psalm of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I call to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; hurry to me; give ear to my voice when I call to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: A psalm of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I am calling to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; come to me quickly. Hear my voice as I cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: A song of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I am calling to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Please come quickly and help me. Listen to me when I call out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: hurry to me: come quickly to help
decisions.reason: The same plea opens 22:20, 38:23 and 70:2: come quickly, because the danger is near.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1.

decisions.choice: and help me
decisions.reason: Readable says why the psalmist asks God to come quickly (m2).

source.text: תִּכּ֤וֹן תְּפִלָּתִ֣י קְטֹ֣רֶת לְפָנֶ֑יךָ מַֽשְׂאַ֥ת כַּ֝פַּ֗י מִנְחַת־עָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: May it be set, my prayer, [as] incense before you, [the] lifting of my palms [as an] offering of evening.

en.L: Let my prayer be set [as] incense before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the lifting up of my hands [as the] evening offering.
en.B: Let my prayer stand before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} like incense, my lifted hands like the offering at evening.
en.R: Let my prayer come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} like the sweet smoke of incense. Let my hands, raised to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in prayer, be like the offering given each evening.

decisions.choice: incense and the evening offering
decisions.reason: Each morning and evening incense was burned before the LORD (Exodus 30:7-8), and a lamb with a grain offering (minchah) was offered each evening (Exodus 29:38-41). The psalmist asks that his prayer be received as those offerings were. Daniel prayed at the time of the evening offering (Daniel 9:21).

decisions.choice: be set: be accepted, stand firm before God
decisions.reason: The verb (kun) means to be set firm or established: may his prayer be accepted and stand before God.

decisions.choice: lifting of my palms: raising the hands in prayer
decisions.reason: People prayed standing with hands raised and palms open toward God (28:2; 63:5; 134:2).

decisions.choice: the sweet smoke of incense
decisions.reason: Readable says what incense is: spices burned for their sweet smoke.

source.text: שִׁיתָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה שָׁמְרָ֣ה לְפִ֑י נִ֝צְּרָ֗ה עַל־דַּ֥ל שְׂפָתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Set, YHWH, a guard for my mouth; keep watch over [the] door of my lips.

en.L: Set, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, a guard for my mouth; keep watch over [the] door of my lips.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, station a guard at my mouth; keep a sentry at the doorway of my lips.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, guard my mouth. Keep watch over my lips, so that I do not say what I should not.

decisions.choice: the door of my lips: what comes out of the mouth
decisions.reason: The mouth is pictured as a city gate with a guard on watch. The psalmist asks God to keep him from speaking evil (39:2), unlike the wicked of verse 4.

decisions.choice: door: the door itself, or its threshold
decisions.reason: The word (dal) is the door or the leaf of a door; it is found only here in this form.

decisions.choice: so that I do not say what I should not
decisions.reason: Readable says what the guard is for (m1).

source.text: אַל־תַּט־לִבִּ֨י לְדָבָ֪ר׀רָ֡ע לְהִתְע֘וֹלֵ֤ל עֲלִל֨וֹת׀בְּרֶ֗שַׁע אֶת־אִישִׁ֥ים פֹּֽעֲלֵי־אָ֑וֶן וּבַל־אֶ֝לְחַ֗ם בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not incline my heart to a thing evil, to busy [myself with] deeds in wickedness with men doing iniquity; and let me not eat of their delicacies.

en.L: Do not turn my heart to an evil thing, to busy [myself with] deeds in wickedness with {{gender:people|men}} who do iniquity; and let me not eat of their delicacies.
en.B: Keep my heart from leaning toward anything evil, from joining with wrongdoers in their wicked acts; let me not share their rich food.
en.R: Do not let me want to do anything evil. Keep me from joining wicked people in the bad things they do. Do not let me enjoy their fancy feasts.

decisions.choice: their delicacies: the good things the wicked enjoy
decisions.reason: To eat at someone's table was to share their life and take their side. The psalmist refuses the rewards of joining the wicked (Proverbs 4:17; 23:1-3).

decisions.choice: busy myself with deeds: take part in doings
decisions.reason: The verb and noun come from the same root ('alal): to act, to carry out deeds. Here they are deeds done in wickedness.

decisions.choice: do not incline my heart: keep me from wanting evil
decisions.reason: The psalmist asks God to guard not only his mouth (verse 3) but what he wants and loves (119:36).

decisions.choice: wrongdoers; wicked people
decisions.reason: "Men" here means people of any kind who do wrong (po'ale 'awen, as in 5:6), so Balanced and Readable name them without it.

source.text: יֶֽהֶלְמֵֽנִי־צַדִּ֨יק׀חֶ֡סֶד וְֽיוֹכִיחֵ֗נִי שֶׁ֣מֶן רֹ֭אשׁ אַל־יָנִ֣י רֹאשִׁ֑י כִּי־ע֥וֹד וּ֝תְפִלָּתִ֗י בְּרָעוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Let him strike me, [the] righteous — loyal love; and let him rebuke me — oil of head; not let it refuse, my head; for still my prayer [is] against their evils.

en.L: Let [the] righteous strike me — [it is] loyal love; and let {{gender:them|him}} rebuke me — [it is] oil for [the] head; let my head not refuse [it]. For still my prayer [is] against their evil deeds.
en.B: Let a righteous person strike me: that is loyal love. Let them reprove me: that is oil for my head, and may my head never refuse it. But all the while I pray against the evil they do.
en.R: If good people hit me to correct me, it is because they care about me. If they warn me, it is like a gift of oil on my head, and I will not turn it away. But I keep praying against the evil that wicked people do.

decisions.choice: oil for the head: the Hebrew text
alternatives: let the oil of a sinner not anoint my head (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: This verse is hard and its text may have suffered in copying. The ancient Greek translation reads "let not the oil of a sinner anoint my head", which fits verse 4. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: oil for the head: a welcome kindness
decisions.reason: Oil was poured on the head of an honored guest (23:5; Luke 7:46). A rebuke from a righteous person is as welcome as that honor (Proverbs 27:6).

decisions.choice: loyal love: faithful, committed love
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith with a bond or covenant. It is "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced and "faithful love" at Readable, as in 5:8.

decisions.choice: their evil deeds: those of the wicked
alternatives: against their evil deeds (of the righteous)
decisions.reason: "Their" most likely points back to the wrongdoers of verse 4: the psalmist keeps praying against what they do.

decisions.choice: a righteous person ... them (B); good people (R)
decisions.reason: The righteous person here is anyone who does right, so Balanced and Readable use words that include men and women.

decisions.choice: because they care about me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the loyal love of a friend who corrects means here (m3).

source.text: נִשְׁמְט֣וּ בִֽידֵי־סֶ֭לַע שֹׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם וְשָׁמְע֥וּ אֲ֝מָרַ֗י כִּ֣י נָעֵֽמוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: They have been thrown down by [the] hands of [the] rock, their judges, and they will hear my words, for they are pleasant.

en.L: Their judges have been thrown down by [the] sides of [the] cliff, and they will hear my words, for they are pleasant.
en.B: When their rulers are flung down the face of the cliff, people will hear my words and know that they were kind.
en.R: When their leaders are thrown off the cliff, people will listen to me. They will see that my words were good.

decisions.choice: a picture of judgment on the wicked rulers
alternatives: their judges were thrown down, yet they heard my words
when they fall into the hands of the Rock (God), their judges will hear
decisions.reason: This verse and the next are among the hardest in the Psalms. The likely sense is that when the leaders of the wicked are judged, others will see that the psalmist's words were true and gentle. Who "they" are who hear is not said.

decisions.choice: thrown down the cliff: a form of execution
decisions.reason: Enemies were sometimes put to death by being thrown from a cliff (2 Chronicles 25:12; Luke 4:29).

decisions.choice: their judges: their rulers
decisions.reason: The word (shofet) is a judge or ruler, here the leaders of the wicked.

decisions.choice: people will hear
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "people", since "they" cannot be the leaders who have fallen (m1).

source.text: כְּמ֤וֹ פֹלֵ֣חַ וּבֹקֵ֣עַ בָּאָ֑רֶץ נִפְזְר֥וּ עֲ֝צָמֵ֗ינוּ לְפִ֣י שְׁאֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: As one plowing and breaking up in the earth, they have been scattered, our bones, at [the] mouth of Sheol.

en.L: As [when] one plows and breaks up the earth, our bones have been scattered at [the] mouth of Sheol.
en.B: Like clods when the ground is plowed and broken open, our bones lie scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
en.R: Our bones are scattered at the door of the place of the dead, like lumps of earth turned up by a plow.

decisions.choice: our bones: the Hebrew text
alternatives: their bones (some manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "our bones": the psalmist and those with him are close to death. Some manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation have "their bones", which would continue the judgment of verse 6.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the world of the dead, pictured as a mouth that swallows (Isaiah 5:14). The bones lie at its opening.

decisions.choice: like one plowing: scattered like broken earth
decisions.reason: The picture is of clods thrown up and left lying by the plow.

decisions.choice: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: As in 6:6.

source.text: כִּ֤י אֵלֶ֨יךָ׀יְהֹוִ֣ה אֲדֹנָ֣י עֵינָ֑י בְּכָ֥ה חָ֝סִ֗יתִי אַל־תְּעַ֥ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: For to you, YHWH [the] Lord, [are] my eyes; in you I take refuge; do not pour out my soul.

en.L: For to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} my Lord, [are] my eyes; in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I take refuge; do not pour out my soul.
en.B: But my eyes look to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}; I make {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} my refuge. Do not let my life be poured out.
en.R: But Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I am looking to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help. I run to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for safety. Do not let me die.

decisions.choice: GOD my Lord
decisions.reason: As in 140:8.

decisions.choice: pour out my soul: let my life drain away to death
decisions.reason: The verb ('arah) means to lay bare or empty out. To pour out the soul is to die (Isaiah 53:12).

decisions.choice: to you are my eyes: I look to you for help
decisions.reason: Eyes turned toward someone wait on them for help (25:15; 123:1-2).

decisions.choice: GOD my Lord (L); Lord GOD (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 140:8.

decisions.choice: do not let me die
alternatives: do not pour out my soul
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

source.text: שָׁמְרֵ֗נִי מִ֣ידֵי פַ֭ח יָ֣קְשׁוּ לִ֑י וּ֝מֹקְשׁ֗וֹת פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: Keep me from [the] hands of [the] trap [that] they have laid for me, and [the] snares of those doing iniquity.

en.L: Keep me from [the] hands of [the] trap [that] they have laid for me, and [from the] snares of those who do iniquity.
en.B: Guard me from the grip of the trap they have set for me, from the snares of those who do wrong.
en.R: Keep me safe from the traps they have set to catch me. Protect me from the snares of people who do evil.

decisions.choice: the hands of the trap: the trap's grip
decisions.reason: The trap is pictured as having hands that seize. As in 140:6, the enemies are hunters setting traps.

decisions.choice: those who do iniquity: wrongdoers
decisions.reason: As in verse 4 (po'ale 'awen).

source.text: יִפְּל֣וּ בְמַכְמֹרָ֣יו רְשָׁעִ֑ים יַ֥חַד אָ֝נֹכִ֗י עַֽד־אֶעֱבֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Let them fall into his nets, [the] wicked, together, while I pass by.

en.L: Let [the] wicked fall into their own nets together, while I pass by.
en.B: May the wicked be caught together in their own nets, while I make my way past.
en.R: Let all those evil people get caught in their own traps, while I get away safely.

decisions.choice: his nets: each one's own nets
decisions.reason: "His nets" is singular: each wicked person falls into the net he set for others (7:16; 9:16; 35:8).

decisions.choice: together: all of them at once
decisions.reason: The word (yachad) can go with the wicked, "all together", or with "I", "while I alone pass by".

decisions.choice: their own nets
decisions.reason: Every level says "their", since "his" here means each of the wicked (m1), not God.

decisions.choice: get away safely
decisions.reason: Readable says what passing by means here: going on unharmed.
